maven_package_requests_forwarding.description: If `true`, forwards Maven package requests to `repo.maven.apache.org` when not found in the GitLab package registry. Premium and Ultimate only.

max_artifacts_size.description: Maximum file size, in MB, for each job's artifacts.

max_decompressed_archive_size.description: Maximum decompressed file size for imported archives in MB. Set to `0` for unlimited. Default is `25600`.

max_github_response_json_value_count.description: Maximum object count for GitHub API responses. Set to `0` for unlimited. The count is an estimate based on the number of `:`, `,`, `{`, and `[` characters in the response.

max_github_response_size_limit.description: Maximum size in MB for GitHub API responses. Set to `0` for unlimited size.

max_http_decompressed_size.description: Maximum allowed size in MiB for Gzip-compressed HTTP responses from outbound requests after decompression. Set to `0` for unlimited.

max_http_response_csv_structural_chars.description: Maximum allowed object count in CSV HTTP responses from outbound requests. Count is an estimate based on the number of `,`, `;`, `\t`, and `\n` occurrences in the response. Introduced in GitLab 18.4.

max_http_response_json_depth.description: Maximum allowed nesting depth in JSON HTTP responses from outbound requests.

max_http_response_json_structural_chars.description: Maximum allowed object count in JSON HTTP responses from outbound requests. Count is an estimate based on the number of `:`, `,`, `{`, and `[` occurrences in the response. Introduced in GitLab 18.4.

max_http_response_size_limit.description: Maximum allowed size in MiB for HTTP responses from outbound requests. Set to `0` for unlimited. Applicable for integrations, importers, and webhooks. Introduced in GitLab 18.4.

max_http_response_xml_structural_chars.description: Maximum allowed object count in XML HTTP responses from outbound requests. Count is an estimate based on the number of `<`, and `=` occurrences in the response. Introduced in GitLab 18.4.

max_import_remote_file_size.description: Maximum remote file size in MB for imports from external object storages

max_login_attempts.description: Maximum number of sign-in attempts before locking out the user.

max_number_of_repository_downloads.description: Maximum number of unique repositories a user can download in the specified time period before they are banned. Default: 0, Maximum: 10,000 repositories. GitLab Self-Managed, Ultimate only.

max_number_of_repository_downloads_withi.description: Reporting time period (in seconds). Default: 0, Maximum: 864000 seconds (10 days). GitLab Self-Managed, Ultimate only.

max_pages_custom_domains_per_project.description: Maximum number of GitLab Pages custom domains per project

max_pages_size.description: Maximum size of each GitLab Pages site in MB. Set to `0` to allow up to 1 TB.

max_personal_access_token_lifetime.description: Maximum allowable lifetime for access tokens in days. When left blank, default value of 365 is applied. When set, value must be 365 or less. When changed, existing access tokens with an expiration date beyond the maximum allowable lifetime are revoked. GitLab Self-Managed, Ultimate only. In GitLab 17.6 or later, the maximum lifetime limit can be [extended to 400 days](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/461901) by enabling a [feature flag](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/feature_flags/) named `buffered_token_expiration_limit`.

max_ssh_key_lifetime.description: Maximum allowable lifetime for SSH keys in days. GitLab Self-Managed, Ultimate only. In GitLab 17.6 or later, the maximum lifetime limit can be [extended to 400 days](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/461901) by enabling a [feature flag](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/feature_flags/) named `buffered_token_expiration_limit`.

max_terraform_state_size_bytes.description: Maximum size of the Terraform state file in bytes. Set to `0` for unlimited size.

max_yaml_depth.description: Maximum depth of nested CI/CD configuration added with the [`include` keyword](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/yaml/#include). Default: `100`.

max_yaml_size_bytes.description: Maximum size in bytes of a single CI/CD configuration file. Default: `2097152`.

merge_requests_create_limit.description: Maximum number of merge requests a user can create per minute. Default: `0`, which disables the rate limit. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/606714) in GitLab 19.6.

merge_requests_merge_ref_limit.description: Maximum number of merge ref requests per minute for each user or IP address. Default: `0`, which disables the rate limit. Introduced in GitLab 19.7.

merge_requests_read_diffs_limit.description: Maximum number of merge request changes, diffs, raw diffs, and diff version API requests per minute for each user, or for each IP address for unauthenticated requests. Default: `300`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/606717) in GitLab 19.7.

merge_requests_rebase_limit.description: Maximum number of merge request rebases per minute for each user. Default: `30`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/606716) in GitLab 19.6.

merge_train_removal_limit_per_user.description: Maximum number of merge requests a user can remove from merge trains per minute. Default: `30`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit.

metrics_method_call_threshold.description: Method call is only tracked if it takes longer than this threshold, in milliseconds.

minimum_language_server_version.description: Minimum language server version to accept requests from.

minimum_password_length.description: Indicates whether passwords require a minimum length. Premium and Ultimate only.

mirror_available.description: If `true`, project Maintainers can configure repository mirroring. If `false`, only administrators can configure repository mirroring.

mirror_capacity_threshold.description: Minimum capacity to be available before scheduling more mirrors preemptively. Premium and Ultimate only.

mirror_max_capacity.description: Maximum number of mirrors that can be synchronizing at the same time. Premium and Ultimate only.

mirror_max_delay.description: Maximum time (in minutes) between updates that a mirror can have when scheduled to synchronize. Premium and Ultimate only.

namespace_aggregation_schedule_lease_dur.description: Maximum duration, in seconds, between refreshes of namespace statistics. Defaults to `300`.

notify_on_unknown_sign_in.description: If `true`, sends a notification when a sign-in from an unknown IP address occurs.

npm_package_requests_forwarding.description: If `true`, forwards npm package requests to `npmjs.org` when not found in the GitLab package registry. Premium and Ultimate only.

o11y_provisioner_api_key.description: API key GitLab sends to the Observability provisioner. GitLab.com only. Not returned in responses.

o11y_provisioner_url.description: URL of the Observability provisioner API. GitLab.com only.

oauth_access_token_expires_in.description: Maximum lifetime in seconds of all new OAuth access tokens issued by the instance. Minimum value: `300` (5 minutes). Default value: `7200` (2 hours). If blank or `null`, uses default value. Does not affect existing OAuth access tokens.

offline_transfer_exports_enabled.description: If `true`, enables exporting GitLab groups and projects by offline transfer. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/588971) in GitLab 19.3.

offline_transfer_imports_enabled.description: If `true`, enables importing GitLab groups and projects by offline transfer. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/588971) in GitLab 19.3.

orbit_indexing_status_limit.description: Maximum number of GitLab Orbit indexing status requests per minute per user. Default: `30`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit.

orbit_item_counts_limit.description: Maximum number of GitLab Orbit item count requests per minute per user. Default: `30`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit.

orbit_query_limit.description: Maximum number of GitLab Orbit queries per minute per user. Default: `60`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit.

orbit_rate_limit_allowlist_raw.description: Raw newline-, comma-, or whitespace-separated list of usernames excluded from the GitLab Orbit rate limits. Maximum: 100 usernames.

outbound_local_requests_whitelist.description: List of trusted domains or IP addresses to which local requests are allowed when local requests for webhooks and integrations are disabled.

package_metadata_purl_types.description: List of [package registry metadata to sync](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/settings/security_and_compliance/#choose-package-registry-metadata-to-sync). See [the list](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/ace16c20d5da7c4928dd03fb139692638b557fe3/app/models/concerns/enums/package_metadata.rb#L5) of the available values. GitLab Self-Managed, Ultimate only.

package_registry_allow_anyone_to_pull_op.description: If `true`, makes the option to [allow anyone to pull from the package registry](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/package_registry/#allow-anyone-to-pull-from-package-registry) visible and changeable in project settings.

package_registry_cleanup_policies_worker.description: Number of workers assigned to the packages cleanup policies.

pages_domain_create_limit.description: Maximum number of Pages custom domains each user can create per day. Default: `20`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/635642) in GitLab 19.6.

pages_domain_verification_enabled.description: If `true`, requires users to prove ownership of custom domains. Domain verification is an essential security measure for public GitLab sites. Users are required to demonstrate they control a domain before it is enabled.

pages_domain_verify_limit.description: Maximum number of Pages custom domain verification requests per minute for each user. Default: `5`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/635642) in GitLab 19.6.

pages_unique_domain_default_enabled.description: If `true`, enables unique domains by default for Pages sites to avoid cookie sharing between sites under a given namespace. Defaults to `true`.

password_authentication_enabled.description: Flag indicating if password authentication is enabled for the web interface. Mutually exclusive with `password_authentication_enabled_for_web`, `signin_enabled`.

password_authentication_enabled_for_git.description: If `true`, enables authentication for Git over HTTP(S) via a GitLab account password. Defaults to `true`.

password_authentication_enabled_for_web.description: If `true`, enables authentication for the web interface via a GitLab account password. Defaults to `true`. Mutually exclusive with `password_authentication_enabled`, `signin_enabled`.

password_lowercase_required.description: If `true`, passwords require at least one lowercase letter. Premium and Ultimate only.

password_number_required.description: If `true`, passwords require at least one number. Premium and Ultimate only.

password_symbol_required.description: If `true`, passwords require at least one symbol character. Premium and Ultimate only.

password_uppercase_required.description: If `true`, passwords require at least one uppercase letter. Premium and Ultimate only.

performance_bar_allowed_group_id.description: Path of the group that is allowed to toggle the performance bar. Deprecated. Use `performance_bar_allowed_group_path` instead.

performance_bar_allowed_group_path.description: Path of the group that is allowed to toggle the performance bar.

performance_bar_enabled.description: Deprecated: Pass `performance_bar_allowed_group_path: nil` instead. Allow enabling the performance.

personal_access_token_prefix.description: Prefix to prepend to all personal access tokens.

pipeline_cancel_limit_per_user_project.description: Maximum number of pipeline cancellations allowed per minute for a given project.

pipeline_delete_limit_per_user_project.description: Maximum number of pipeline deletions allowed per minute for a given project.

pipeline_limit_per_project_user_sha.description: Maximum number of pipeline creation requests per minute per user and commit. Set to `0` for unlimited requests. Disabled by default.

pipeline_limit_per_user.description: Maximum number of pipeline creation requests allowed per minute per user. Set to `0` for unlimited requests.

pipeline_retry_limit_per_user_project.description: Maximum number of pipeline retries allowed per minute for a given project.

pipeline_schedule_management_limit_per_u.description: Maximum number of pipeline schedule changes (create, update, delete, take ownership) allowed per minute for a given user.

pipeline_trigger_management_limit_per_us.description: Maximum number of pipeline trigger token changes (create, update, delete) allowed per minute for a given user.

plantuml_diagram_proxy_enabled.description: Enable PlantUML diagram proxy. Default is `false`.

polling_interval_multiplier.description: Interval multiplier used by endpoints that perform polling. Set to `0` to disable polling.

prevent_merge_requests_author_approval.description: If `true`, prevents merge request authors from approving their own merge requests.

prevent_merge_requests_committers_approv.description: If `true`, prevents committers from approving merge requests they contributed to.

project_audit_events_api_limit.description: Maximum number of requests per minute per user per project to the project audit events API.

project_export_limit_per_root_namespace.description: Maximum number of project export requests every 10 minutes for each top-level group or personal namespace, across all its projects. Default: 0. Set to `0` for no limit.

project_hooks_create_limit.description: Maximum number of project webhooks a user can create per minute for a given project. Default: `5`. Set to `0` to disable limits. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/605597) in GitLab 19.6.

project_jobs_api_rate_limit.description: Maximum authenticated requests to /project/:id/jobs per minute

project_relations_export_download_limit.description: Maximum number of project relations export downloads per minute per user for each project during direct transfer migrations. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit.

project_relations_export_limit.description: Maximum number of project relations export requests per minute per user for each project during direct transfer migrations. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit.

project_runner_token_expiration_interval.description: Set the expiration time (in seconds) of authentication tokens of newly registered project runners. Minimum value is 7200 seconds. For more information, see [Automatically rotate authentication tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/runners/configure_runners/#automatically-rotate-runner-authentication-tokens).

project_secrets_limit.description: Maximum number of secrets allowed per project in Secrets Manager. Default: 100. To disable the limit, set to `0`. Ultimate only. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/219436) in GitLab 18.9.

projects_api_rate_limit_unauthenticated.description: Maximum number of requests per 10 minutes per IP address for unauthenticated requests to the [list all projects API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/projects/#list-all-projects). Default: `400`. To disable throttling, set to `0`.

protected_ci_variables.description: If `true`, CI/CD variables are protected by default.

push_event_activities_limit.description: Maximum number of changes (branches or tags) in a single push above which a bulk push event is created. Setting to `0` does not disable throttling.

push_event_hooks_limit.description: Maximum number of changes (branches or tags) in a single push above which webhooks and integrations are not triggered. Setting to `0` does not disable throttling. Default: `3`.

pypi_package_requests_forwarding.description: If `true`, forwards PyPI package requests to `pypi.org` when not found in the GitLab package registry. Premium and Ultimate only.

rate_limiting_response_text.description: When rate limiting is enabled via the `throttle_*` settings, send this plain text response when a rate limit is exceeded. `Retry later` is sent if this is blank.

raw_blob_request_limit.description: Maximum number of requests per minute for each raw path (default is `300`). Set to `0` to disable throttling.

raw_blob_request_limit_unauthenticated.description: Maximum number of unauthenticated requests per minute across all raw paths in a project (default is `800`). Set to `0` to disable throttling.

receptive_cluster_agents_enabled.description: If `true`, enables receptive mode for GitLab agents for Kubernetes.

relation_export_batch_size.description: Size of each batch when exporting batched relations. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/194607) in GitLab 18.2.

release_evidence_collections_limit_per_u.description: Maximum number of release evidence collection requests a user can make per minute. Set to `0` to disable the limit.

release_evidence_max_size_bytes.description: Maximum size of a release evidence, in bytes. Applies only when the `release_evidence_size_limit` feature flag is enabled. Default: `2097152` (2 MiB). To disable the limit, set to `0`.

release_writes_limit_per_project.description: Maximum number of release create and update requests per minute for each project. Set to `0` to disable the limit.

release_writes_limit_per_user.description: Maximum number of release create and update requests a user can make per minute. Set to `0` to disable the limit.

repository_checks_enabled.description: If `true`, GitLab periodically runs `git fsck` in all project and wiki repositories to look for silent disk corruption issues.

repository_size_limit.description: Size limit per repository (MB). Premium and Ultimate only.

repository_storages_weighted.description: Hash of names of storages taken from `gitlab.yml` to [weights](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/repository_storage_paths/#configure-where-new-repositories-are-stored) ranging from 0 to 100. New projects are created in one of these stores, chosen by a weighted random selection.

require_admin_approval_after_user_signup.description: If `true`, requires explicit administrator approval for new signups.

require_admin_two_factor_authentication.description: Allow administrators to require 2FA for all administrators on the instance.

require_email_verification_on_account_lo.description: If `true`, all users on the instance must verify their identity after suspicious sign-in activity is detected.

require_personal_access_token_expiry.description: If `true`, requires an expiration date on group and project access tokens, and on personal access tokens not owned by service accounts.

require_sha_for_merge.description: If `true`, requires a valid commit `sha` for calls to the [merge a merge request](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/merge_requests/#merge-a-merge-request) endpoint. Sets the instance default. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/236732) in GitLab 19.2.

require_two_factor_authentication.description: If `true`, requires all users to set up two-factor authentication. Requires `two_factor_grace_period`.

resource_usage_limits.description: Definition for resource usage limits enforced in Sidekiq workers.

restricted_visibility_levels.description: Selected levels cannot be used by non-administrator users for groups, projects, or snippets. Can take `private`, `internal`, and `public` as a parameter. If the `public` level is restricted, user profiles are only visible to signed-in users. If empty, no levels are restricted. Cannot select levels that are set as `default_project_visibility` and `default_group_visibility`.

rsa_key_restriction.description: Restrictions on the complexity of uploaded RSA keys. A value of -1 disables all RSA keys.

rubygems_package_requests_forwarding.description: If `true`, forwards RubyGems package requests to `rubygems.org` when not found in the GitLab package registry. Premium and Ultimate only.

runner_job_list_completed_statuses_limit.description: Maximum number of runner job list requests filtered by a completed status allowed per minute for a given user.

runner_job_list_project_filtered_limit_p.description: Maximum number of runner job list requests filtered to the user's projects allowed per minute for a given user.

runner_jobs_endpoints_api_limit.description: Maximum number of requests per minute per job token for requests to the `/jobs/*` runner jobs API endpoints. Default: `200`. To disable throttling, set to `0`. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/462537) in GitLab 18.5.

runner_jobs_patch_trace_api_limit.description: Maximum number of requests per minute per runner token for requests to the `PATCH /jobs/:id/trace` runner jobs API endpoint. Default: 2000. To disable throttling, set to 0. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/462537) in GitLab 18.5.

runner_jobs_request_api_limit.description: Maximum number of requests per minute per runner token for requests to the `/jobs/request` runner jobs API endpoint. Default: `2000`. To disable throttling, set to `0`. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/462537) in GitLab 18.5.

runner_manager_creation_limit.description: Maximum number of runner managers each runner can create every 10 minutes. Applies only when the `log_runner_manager_creation_limit` or `enforce_runner_manager_creation_limit` feature flag is enabled. Default: `1000`. To disable the limit, set to `0`.

runner_manager_list_limit_per_user.description: Maximum number of runner managers a user can list per minute.

runner_token_expiration_interval.description: Set the expiration time (in seconds) of authentication tokens of newly registered instance runners. Minimum value is 7200 seconds. For more information, see [Automatically rotate authentication tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/runners/configure_runners/#automatically-rotate-runner-authentication-tokens).

scan_execution_policies_action_limit.description: Maximum number of `actions` per scan execution policy. Defaults to `0` and cannot be set above `20`.

scan_execution_policies_schedule_limit.description: Maximum number of `type: schedule` rules per scan execution policy. Defaults to `0` and cannot be set above `20`.

search_rate_limit.description: Maximum number of requests per minute for performing a search while authenticated. Default: `30`. To disable throttling, set to `0`.

search_rate_limit_unauthenticated.description: Maximum number of requests per minute for performing a search while unauthenticated. Default: `10`. To disable throttling, set to `0`.

secret_detection_revocation_token_types_.description: URL that returns the token types that can be revoked.

secret_detection_token_revocation_enable.description: If `true`, enables secret detection token revocation.

secret_detection_token_revocation_url.description: URL that GitLab sends leaked tokens to for revocation.

secret_push_protection_available.description: If `true`, allows projects to enable secret push protection. This does not enable secret push protection. Ultimate only.

security_approval_policies_limit.description: Maximum number of active merge request approval policies per security policy project. Defaults to `5` and cannot be set above `20`.

security_mr_report_cache_lifetime_minute.description: Number of minutes to cache security reports on merge requests (10-60). Default: 10. Premium and Ultimate only. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/223399) in GitLab 18.10.

security_policy_global_group_approvers_e.description: If `true`, looks up merge request approval policy approval groups globally. If `false`, looks them up within project hierarchies.

security_scan_stale_after_days.description: Number of days to retain security scan data before purging. Must be between 7 and 90 days. Default: 30 days for GitLab.com, 90 days for GitLab Self-Managed. Premium and Ultimate only. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/222998) in GitLab 18.9.

security_txt_content.description: Public security contact information made available at https://gitlab.example.com/.well-known/security.txt.

service_access_tokens_expiration_enforce.description: If `true`, enforces token expiration for service account users. Premium and Ultimate only.

session_expire_delay.description: Session duration in minutes. Requires a GitLab restart to apply changes.

session_expire_from_init.description: If `true`, sessions expire a number of minutes after the session was created rather than after the last activity. The session lifetime is defined by `session_expire_delay`.

shared_runners_enabled.description: Enable shared runners for new projects

shared_runners_minutes.description: Set the maximum number of compute minutes that a group can use on instance runners per month. Premium and Ultimate only.

show_migrate_from_jenkins_banner.description: If `true`, shows the Jenkins migration banner.

sidekiq_job_limiter_compression_threshol.description: Threshold in bytes at which Sidekiq jobs are compressed before being stored in Redis. Default: 100,000 bytes (100 KB).

sidekiq_job_limiter_limit_bytes.description: Threshold in bytes at which Sidekiq jobs are rejected. Default: 0 bytes (doesn't reject any job).

sidekiq_job_limiter_mode.description: Sets the behavior for Sidekiq job size limits. Default: 'compress'.

sidekiq_timezone_override.description: IANA timezone identifier (for example, `America/Chicago`) applied to all Sidekiq cron jobs. When blank, no override is applied and cron jobs use the Rails application timezone.

signin_enabled.description: If `true`, enables password authentication for the web interface. Deprecated. Use `password_authentication_enabled_for_web` instead. Mutually exclusive with `password_authentication_enabled_for_web`, `password_authentication_enabled`.

slack_app_enabled.description: If `true`, enables the GitLab for Slack app. Requires `slack_app_id`, `slack_app_secret`, `slack_app_signing_secret`, and `slack_app_verification_token`.

slack_app_id.description: Client ID of the GitLab for Slack app.

slack_app_secret.description: Client secret of the GitLab for Slack app. Used for authenticating OAuth requests from the app.

slack_app_signing_secret.description: Signing secret of the GitLab for Slack app. Used for authenticating API requests from the app.

slack_app_verification_token.description: Verification token of the GitLab for Slack app. This method of authentication is deprecated by Slack and used only for authenticating slash commands from the app.

snippet_size_limit.description: Maximum snippet content size in bytes. Default: 52428800 bytes (50 MB).

snowplow_app_id.description: Snowplow site name or application ID, for example `gitlab`.

snowplow_database_collector_hostname.description: The Snowplow collector for database events hostname. (for example, `your-db-snowplow-collector.example.com`)

sourcegraph_public_only.description: If `true`, blocks Sourcegraph from being loaded on private and internal projects. Defaults to `true`.

spam_check_api_key.description: API key used by GitLab for accessing the Spam Check service endpoint.

spam_check_endpoint_enabled.description: Enable Spam Check via external API endpoint

spam_check_endpoint_url.description: URL of the external Spamcheck service endpoint. Valid URI schemes are `grpc` or `tls`. Specifying `tls` forces communication to be encrypted.

static_objects_external_storage_auth_tok.description: Authentication token for the external storage linked in `static_objects_external_storage_url`.

static_objects_external_storage_url.description: URL to an external storage for repository static objects.

subscription_usage_per_day_limit.description: Maximum number of `subscriptionUsage` and `trialUsage` GraphQL requests per day per user. Default: `40000`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit.

subscription_usage_per_hour_limit.description: Maximum number of `subscriptionUsage` and `trialUsage` GraphQL requests per hour per user. Default: `10000`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit.

subscription_usage_per_minute_limit.description: Maximum number of `subscriptionUsage` and `trialUsage` GraphQL requests per minute per user. Default: `300`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit.

subscriptions_payment_form_per_hour_limi.description: Maximum number of payment form requests per hour per authenticated user, or per IP address during identity verification. Default: `20`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit.

subscriptions_validate_payment_method_pe.description: Maximum number of payment method validation requests per hour per authenticated user, or per IP address during identity verification. Default: `10`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit.

system_hooks_create_limit.description: Maximum number of system hooks a user can create per minute. Default: `5`. Set to `0` to disable limits. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/635281) in GitLab 19.6.

terminal_max_session_time.description: Maximum time for a web terminal WebSocket connection, in seconds. Set to `0` for unlimited time.

terms.description: (**Required by**: `enforce_terms`) Markdown content for the ToS.

terraform_state_encryption_enabled.description: Enable encryption for Terraform state files

throttle_authenticated_api_enabled.description: If `true`, enables the authenticated API request rate limit. Helps reduce request volume (for example, from crawlers or abusive bots). Requires `throttle_authenticated_api_period_in_seconds` and `throttle_authenticated_api_requests_per_period`.

throttle_authenticated_api_requests_per_.description: Maximum requests per period per user.

throttle_authenticated_dependency_proxy_.description: If `true`, enforces the authenticated dependency proxy request rate limit. Default value: `false`.
Rate limit period in seconds. `throttle_authenticated_dependency_proxy_enabled` must be `true`. Default value: `15`.
Maximum requests per period per user. `throttle_authenticated_dependency_proxy_enabled` must be `true`. Default value: `1000`.

throttle_authenticated_git_http_enabled.description: If `true`, enforces the authenticated Git HTTP request rate limit. Default value: `false`.

throttle_authenticated_git_http_period_i.description: Rate limit period in seconds. `throttle_authenticated_git_http_enabled` must be `true`. Default value: `3600`.

throttle_authenticated_git_http_requests.description: Maximum requests per period per user. `throttle_authenticated_git_http_enabled` must be `true`. Default value: `3600`.

throttle_authenticated_mcp_enabled.description: If `true`, enforces the rate limit on requests to the MCP Server endpoint, `/api/v4/mcp`, for any HTTP method. Does not apply to other MCP endpoints. Default value: `false`.

throttle_authenticated_mcp_period_in_sec.description: Rate limit period in seconds. `throttle_authenticated_mcp_enabled` must be `true`. Default value: `60`.

throttle_authenticated_mcp_requests_per_.description: Maximum requests per period per user. `throttle_authenticated_mcp_enabled` must be `true`. Default value: `600`.

throttle_authenticated_packages_api_enab.description: If `true`, enables the authenticated package registry API request rate limit. Helps reduce request volume (for example, from crawlers or abusive bots). View [package registry rate limits](https://docs.gitlab.com/rate_limits/api/package-registry/) for more details. Requires `throttle_authenticated_packages_api_period_in_seconds` and `throttle_authenticated_packages_api_requests_per_period`.

throttle_authenticated_packages_api_peri.description: Rate limit period in seconds. View [package registry rate limits](https://docs.gitlab.com/rate_limits/api/package-registry/) for more details.

throttle_authenticated_packages_api_requ.description: Maximum requests per period per user. View [package registry rate limits](https://docs.gitlab.com/rate_limits/api/package-registry/) for more details.

throttle_authenticated_web_enabled.description: If `true`, enables the authenticated web request rate limit. Helps reduce request volume (for example, from crawlers or abusive bots). Requires `throttle_authenticated_web_period_in_seconds` and `throttle_authenticated_web_requests_per_period`.

throttle_authenticated_web_requests_per_.description: Maximum requests per period per user.

throttle_unauthenticated_api_enabled.description: If `true`, enables the unauthenticated API request rate limit. Helps reduce request volume (for example, from crawlers or abusive bots). Requires `throttle_unauthenticated_api_period_in_seconds` and `throttle_unauthenticated_api_requests_per_period`.

throttle_unauthenticated_api_requests_pe.description: Maximum requests per period per IP.

throttle_unauthenticated_enabled.description: If `true`, enables the unauthenticated web request rate limit. Helps reduce request volume (for example, from crawlers or abusive bots). Requires `throttle_unauthenticated_period_in_seconds` and `throttle_unauthenticated_requests_per_period`. [Deprecated](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/335300) in GitLab 14.3. Use `throttle_unauthenticated_web_enabled` or `throttle_unauthenticated_api_enabled` instead.

throttle_unauthenticated_git_http_enable.description: If `true`, enforces the unauthenticated Git HTTP request rate limit. Default value: `false`.

throttle_unauthenticated_git_http_period.description: Rate limit period in seconds. `throttle_unauthenticated_git_http_enabled` must be `true`. Default value: `3600`.

throttle_unauthenticated_git_http_reques.description: Maximum requests per period per IP. `throttle_unauthenticated_git_http_enabled` must be `true`. Default value: `3600`.

throttle_unauthenticated_packages_api_en.description: If `true`, enables the unauthenticated package registry API request rate limit. Helps reduce request volume (for example, from crawlers or abusive bots). View [package registry rate limits](https://docs.gitlab.com/rate_limits/api/package-registry/) for more details. Requires `throttle_unauthenticated_packages_api_period_in_seconds` and `throttle_unauthenticated_packages_api_requests_per_period`.

throttle_unauthenticated_packages_api_pe.description: Rate limit period in seconds. View [package registry rate limits](https://docs.gitlab.com/rate_limits/api/package-registry/) for more details.

throttle_unauthenticated_packages_api_re.description: Maximum requests per period per IP. View [package registry rate limits](https://docs.gitlab.com/rate_limits/api/package-registry/) for more details.

throttle_unauthenticated_period_in_secon.description: Rate limit period in seconds. [Deprecated](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/335300) in GitLab 14.3. Use `throttle_unauthenticated_web_period_in_seconds` or `throttle_unauthenticated_api_period_in_seconds` instead.

throttle_unauthenticated_requests_per_pe.description: Maximum requests per period per IP. [Deprecated](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/335300) in GitLab 14.3. Use `throttle_unauthenticated_web_requests_per_period` or `throttle_unauthenticated_api_requests_per_period` instead.

throttle_unauthenticated_web_enabled.description: If `true`, enables the unauthenticated web request rate limit. Helps reduce request volume (for example, from crawlers or abusive bots). Requires `throttle_unauthenticated_web_period_in_seconds` and `throttle_unauthenticated_web_requests_per_period`.

throttle_unauthenticated_web_requests_pe.description: Maximum requests per period per IP.

time_tracking_limit_to_hours.description: If `true`, limits display of time tracking units to hours. Default is `false`.

top_level_group_creation_enabled.description: If `true`, users can create top-level groups with the API. Defaults to `true`.

trial_create_limit.description: Maximum number of trial creation requests per hour per user. Default: `10`. Set to `0` to disable the rate limit.

two_factor_grace_period.description: Amount of time, in hours, that users can skip enforced two-factor authentication setup.

unconfirmed_users_delete_after_days.description: Specifies how many days after account creation to delete users who have not confirmed their email. Only applicable if `delete_unconfirmed_users` is set to `true`. Must be `1` or greater. Default is `7`. GitLab Self-Managed, Premium and Ultimate only.

unique_ips_limit_enabled.description: If `true`, limits sign-ins from multiple IP addresses. Requires `unique_ips_limit_per_user` and `unique_ips_limit_time_window`.

unique_ips_limit_per_user.description: Maximum number of IPs per user.

unique_ips_limit_time_window.description: How many seconds an IP is counted towards the limit.

update_runner_versions_enabled.description: If `true`, fetches GitLab Runner release version data from GitLab.com. For more information, see how to [determine which runners need to be upgraded](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/runners/runners_scope/#determine-which-runners-need-to-be-upgraded).

updating_name_disabled_for_users.description: If `true`, prevents users from updating their profile name.

usage_ping_enabled.description: Every week GitLab will report license usage back to GitLab, Inc.

use_clickhouse_for_analytics.description: If `true`, enables ClickHouse as a data source for analytics reports. ClickHouse must be configured for this setting to take effect. Premium and Ultimate only.

use_nats_for_audit_streaming.description: If `true`, routes audit event streaming through NATS JetStream. NATS must be configured for this setting to take effect. Premium and Ultimate only.

user_deactivation_emails_enabled.description: If `true`, sends emails to users when their account is deactivated.

user_default_external.description: If `true`, newly registered users are external by default.

user_default_internal_regex.description: Specify an email address regex pattern to identify default internal users.

user_defaults_to_private_profile.description: If `true`, newly created users have a private profile by default. Defaults to `false`.

user_oauth_applications.description: If `true`, allows users to register any application to use GitLab as an OAuth provider. This setting does not affect group-level OAuth applications.

user_show_add_ssh_key_message.description: When set to `false` disable the `You won't be able to pull or push repositories via SSH until you add an SSH key to your profile` warning shown to users with no uploaded SSH key.

users_api_limit_followers.description: Maximum number of requests per minute, per user or IP address. Default: 100. Set to `0` to disable limits. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/181054) in GitLab 17.10.

users_api_limit_following.description: Maximum number of requests per minute, per user or IP address. Default: 100. Set to `0` to disable limits. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/181054) in GitLab 17.10.

users_api_limit_gpg_key.description: Maximum number of requests per minute, per user or IP address. Default: 120. Set to `0` to disable limits. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/181054) in GitLab 17.10.

users_api_limit_gpg_keys.description: Maximum number of requests per minute, per user or IP address. Default: 120. Set to `0` to disable limits. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/181054) in GitLab 17.10.

users_api_limit_status.description: Maximum number of requests per minute, per user or IP address. Default: 240. Set to `0` to disable limits. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/181054) in GitLab 17.10.

users_get_by_id_limit.description: Maximum number of calls to the `/users/:id` API per 10 minutes per user. Set to `0` for unlimited requests.

valid_runner_registrars.description: List of types which are allowed to register a GitLab Runner. Can be `[]`, `['group']`, `['project']`, or `['group', 'project']`.

version_check_enabled.description: If `true`, GitLab informs you when an update is available.

virtual_registries_endpoints_api_limit.description: Maximum number of requests on virtual registries endpoints, per IP address, per 15 seconds. Default: 4000. To disable limits, set to `0`. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/521692) in GitLab 17.11.

vscode_extension_marketplace.description: Settings for VS Code Extension Marketplace.

custom_values.description: VS Code Extension Marketplace URL's when preset is 'custom'

enabled.description: If `true`, enables the VS Code extension marketplace for the Web IDE and Workspaces.

preset.description: The preset configuration of URL's for the VS Code Extension Marketplace

web_hook_event_resend_limit.description: Maximum number of webhook event resend requests per minute, per user, for a given project or group. Default: `5`. Set to `0` to disable limits. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/587887) in GitLab 19.3.

web_hook_test_limit.description: Maximum number of webhook test requests per minute, per user, for a given project, group, or organization. Default: `5`. Set to `0` to disable limits. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/587887) in GitLab 19.3.

whats_new_variant.description: Which features [What's new](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/whats-new/) shows. `all_tiers` shows features for all tiers, `current_tier` shows only features for the instance's tier, and `disabled` hides What's new.

wiki_asciidoc_allow_uri_includes.description: If `true`, allows URI includes for AsciiDoc wiki pages.

wiki_page_max_content_bytes.description: Maximum wiki page content size in bytes. Default: 5242880 bytes (5 MB). The minimum value is 1024 bytes.

broadcast_type.description: Appearance type of the broadcast message.

color.description: Background color hex code. Deprecated. Use `theme` instead.

dismissable.description: If `true`, the user can dismiss the message.

ends_at.description: Ending time, in UTC. When creating a message, defaults to one hour after the current time.

font.description: Foreground color hex code. Deprecated. Use `theme` instead.

starts_at.description: Starting time, in UTC. When creating a message, defaults to the current time.

target_access_levels.description: Target access levels (roles) of the broadcast message.

target_path.description: Target path of the broadcast message.

theme.description: Color theme for the broadcast message. Applies only to banners.

percentage.description: Percentage of namespaces to enable or disable Elasticsearch indexing for.

plan.description: Subscription tier to rollout Elasticsearch for.

checksum_mismatch_report_threshold.description: Number of consecutive checksum mismatches on a secondary node before it reports the resource to the primary for self-heal re-verification. Read from the secondary node, and has no effect when set on the primary.

checksum_mismatch_self_heal_cooldown_min.description: Minimum time, in minutes, between self-heal re-verification triggers for the same resource. The primary and each secondary node use their own value. Secondary nodes use it to throttle re-reporting the same resource, and the primary uses it to throttle re-verifying an already-verified resource.

container_repositories_max_capacity.description: Maximum concurrency of container repository sync for the node.

enabled.description: If `true`, the Geo node is enabled.

files_max_capacity.description: Maximum concurrency of LFS and attachment backfill for the secondary node.

internal_url.description: URL defined on the primary node that secondary nodes use to contact it. Returns `url` if not set.

minimum_reverification_interval.description: Interval, in days, after which repository verification expires and is repeated. Has no effect when set on a secondary node.

name.description: Unique identifier for the Geo node. Must match `geo_node_name` if it is set in `gitlab.rb`, otherwise it must match `external_url`.

repos_max_capacity.description: Maximum concurrency of repository backfill for the secondary node.

selective_sync_namespace_ids.description: IDs of groups to sync if `selective_sync_type` is `namespaces`.

selective_sync_organization_ids.description: IDs of organizations to sync if `selective_sync_type` is `organizations`.

selective_sync_shards.description: Repository storages to sync projects from if `selective_sync_type` is `shards`.

selective_sync_type.description: Limit syncing to only specific groups or shards. Possible values are `namespaces`, `shards`, and `null`.

sync_object_storage.description: If `true`, the secondary Geo node replicates blobs in object storage.

url.description: User-facing URL of the Geo node.

verification_max_capacity.description: Maximum concurrency of repository verification for the node.

blob_download_timeout.description: Maximum time (in seconds) for blob downloads during Geo sync. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/569919) in GitLab 18.10.

checksum_mismatch_report_threshold.description: Number of consecutive checksum mismatches on a secondary site before it reports the resource to the primary for self-heal re-verification. Read from the secondary site, and has no effect when set on the primary.

checksum_mismatch_self_heal_cooldown_min.description: Minimum time, in minutes, between self-heal re-verification triggers for the same resource. architectures.description: List of architectures of the Debian distribution.

default_branch_protection.description: Determine if developers can push to default branch. `0`: no protection. Users with the Developer or Maintainer role can push new commits, force push, and delete the branch. `1`: partial protection. Users with the Developer or Maintainer role can push new commits. `2`: full protection. Only users with the Maintainer role can push new commits. `3`: protected against pushes. Users with the Maintainer role can push new commits, force push, and accept merge requests. Users with the Developer role can accept merge requests. `4`: full protection after initial push. Users with the Developer role can push commits to an empty repository. Users with the Maintainer role can push new commits and accept merge requests. [Deprecated](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/408314) in GitLab 17.0. Use `default_branch_protection_defaults` instead.

This feature was introduced in GitLab 12.7.

**DEPRECATED**: This endpoint is deprecated and for GitLab.com use only.

This will only ever increase the number of indexed namespaces. Providing a value lower than the current rolled out percentage will have no effect.

This percentage is never persisted but is used to calculate the number of new namespaces to rollout.

If the same percentage is applied again at a later time, due to possible new namespaces being created during the period, some of them will also be indexed. Therefore you may expect that setting this to 10%, then waiting a month and setting to 10% again will trigger new namespaces to be added (i.e. 10% of the number of newly created namespaces in the last month within the given plan).

post.description: Executes a GLQL query to search and filter GitLab resources. Queries are rate limited by the SHA-256 hash of the query. Queries that time out are tracked, and a query that times out too often is temporarily blocked. This feature was introduced in GitLab 18.7.

get.description: Retrieves the GLQL schema: data sources with their filter, display and sort fields, the operator, value kind and reference type vocabularies, the available functions, and the display types a query can be rendered as. The document describes the query language. A query against a data source that is not available to the user fails at `POST /glql`. The document changes only when GitLab is upgraded. It is served with an `ETag`, so clients can send `If-None-Match` to revalidate and receive `304 Not Modified` instead of the full document. The endpoint takes no parameters and returns the same document for every user. Analytics modes list the arguments their dimensions and metrics accept in `parameterized_fields`, so a query can set them explicitly rather than relying on the default. Each entry has a `name` and a `parameters` array. Each parameter has a `name` and a `kind`, and can have `values`, `min`, `max`, `min_days`, `max_days`, `default`, `optional`, `required`, `requires`, `items`, `min_length`, `max_length`, and `strictly_ascending`. This feature was introduced in GitLab 19.3.

Packages of non-public projects are returned only for projects where you have at least the Reporter role. Packages with `processing` status can contain malformed data or be broken. In the response, `creator_id` is the ID of the user who created the package, and is `null` when a deploy token created the package. For a Conan package, `name` contains the recipe, and `conan_package_name` contains the package name. Other package types do not have this field. In `_links`, `web_path` is the path to the package details page in GitLab, returned only if the package has status `default` or `deprecated`, and `delete_api_path` is the API path to delete the package, returned only if you have permission to delete it.

post.description: Imports a repository from Bitbucket Cloud to GitLab. Prerequisites: - The prerequisites for Bitbucket Cloud importer. You must have a Bitbucket Cloud API token with the `read:repository:bitbucket` and `read:pullrequest:bitbucket` scopes. This endpoint shares a rate limit with starting imports from the UI and with file-based project imports. By default, the limit is six requests per minute for each user. An administrator can change this limit in the application settings. This feature was introduced in GitLab 17.0.

Imports a repository from Bitbucket Server to GitLab. The Bitbucket Project Key is only used for finding the repository in Bitbucket. You must specify a `new_namespace` if you want to import the repository to a GitLab group. If you do not specify `new_namespace`, the project imports to your personal user namespace. This endpoint shares a rate limit with starting imports from the UI and with file-based project imports. By default, the limit is six requests per minute for each user. An administrator can change this limit in the application settings.

Imports a repository from GitHub to GitLab. This endpoint shares a rate limit with starting imports from the UI and with file-based project imports. By default, the limit is six requests per minute for each user. An administrator can change this limit in the application settings. The namespace set in `target_namespace` must exist, and must be your user namespace or a group you have the Maintainer or Owner role for. The `optional_stages` hash accepts the keys `attachments_import`, to import Markdown attachments, `collaborators_import`, to import direct repository collaborators who are not outside collaborators, and `continuous_sync`, to keep the project updated from GitHub after the import. `continuous_sync` is only available for github.com. A private GitHub repository is imported as a private project. A public GitHub repository takes the visibility of the target namespace. If that visibility level is restricted, the project uses the default project visibility instead.
Cancels an in-progress import of a GitHub project to GitLab.

Imports personal GitHub gists into GitLab snippets. You can import gists with up to 10 files. GitHub gists with more than 10 files are skipped. You should manually migrate these GitHub gists. If any gists cannot be imported, an email is sent with a list of gists that were not imported. This endpoint has a rate limit of six requests per minute for each user. An administrator can change this limit in the application settings.

post.description: Resolves one Orbit token to a PostgreSQL summary and, optionally, its graph neighborhood. The entity can be a merge request, work item, CI/CD job, CI/CD pipeline, branch, or commit. Requests that reach token resolution count against the orbit_query rate limit; with expand, they run at most one billable graph query. Requires a JSON request body. The request and response shape can change without notice. A `tokens` array that does not hold exactly one string, or an `expand` value that is not the JSON boolean `true` or `false`, returns `400 Bad Request`. With a fine-grained personal access token, the `read_orbit` permission is not enough. The token also needs `read_merge_request` or `read_work_item` on the project or group of the entity, `read_job` on the project for a job and for job logs, `read_pipeline` for pipelines, `read_pipeline_test_report` for failed tests, `read_pipeline_job` for pipeline jobs, `read_branch` or `read_commit` for a branch or commit, `read_commit_diff` and `read_commit_merge_request` for the changed files and merge requests of a commit, and `download_code` for the changed files of a merge request. Without them, the entity is returned as `not_found`. The pipeline status is `null`, and linked items the token cannot read are left out of the summary. Discussions need `read_merge_request_discussion` for a merge request, `read_epic_discussion` for an epic, and `read_issue_discussion` for other work items. Without them, `discussions` is `null`. The project scope of the token applies to the entity summary only. The graph expansion is filtered by the access of the user, the same as for named queries. Token forms are: `Type[id]`, for example `MergeRequest[123]`, where `id` is the global database ID; `gid://gitlab/<Type>/<id>`; a merge request, issue, work item, job, pipeline, or commit URL on this instance, including group work item URLs under `/groups/`; `path!iid` for a merge request, for example `gitlab-org/gitlab!42`; `path#iid` for a work item, for example `gitlab-org/gitlab#7`, where the path can also be a group; `Epic[id]`, `gid://gitlab/Epic/<id>`, an epic URL such as `/groups/gitlab-org/-/epics/5`, or `group&iid`, for example `gitlab-org&5`, where `id` is the epic ID; and `path@ref` for a branch of the project at `path`, or for a commit SHA when no branch has that name, for example `gitlab-org/gitlab@main`. The supported types are `MergeRequest`, `WorkItem`, `Job`, `Pipeline`, `Branch`, and `Commit`. `Issue` is an alias for `WorkItem`, and the response reports `WorkItem`. An epic resolves to its work item in the same way: the response reports `WorkItem`, the ID of the work item, and `work_item_type` `epic`, and the expansion runs for the work item. Other types return `unsupported_type`. Summaries include these fields. For a merge request: title, state, author, branches, head pipeline status, merge commit, reviewers, linked issues, description, changed files with their diffs, failed jobs, and discussions. For a work item: title, state, labels, assignees, milestone, linked merge requests, description, and discussions. For a job: name, status, stage, failure reason, ref, commit, pipeline, merge request, failed tests, and log. For a pipeline: status, ref, commit, source, merge request, jobs, and failed jobs. Jobs come from the pipeline itself, not from its child pipelines. For a branch: head commit, its open or latest merge request, and its latest pipeline with failed jobs. For a commit: title, description, author, its latest pipeline, the merge requests that contain it, and changed files. Failed tests come from the unit test report of the job. The log of a job is its job script output, followed by its `after_script` output, with lines longer than 500 characters cut. The log has a size limit of 40 KB for a requested job and 6 KB for each failed job of a merge request, pipeline, or branch, and `after_script` output gets at most a quarter of it. When a part does not fit, runs of five or more lines that differ only in numbers or hashes, such as progress output, are folded into their first and last line, and only the end of that part that fits is kept. `...` marks where lines were left out, and for a requested job `summary.truncated` then includes `log`. Changed line ranges use new-file line numbers, so a deletion is reported at the line after it, which can be one past the end of the file. A changed file has no `lines` when it was deleted or its diff could not be read, and empty `lines` when its diff has no text lines, such as for a binary or very large file. The `diff` of a changed file has its first 40 diff lines, with 200 lines shared across the merge request in file order. It is absent for deleted, generated, binary, and very large files, and for files after the budget ran out. A cut diff ends with `... N more diff lines`, and `summary.truncated` then includes `diffs`. Lists are limited and contain only records the user can read. `summary.truncated` is an array with the names of the lists that were cut, for example `["reviewers"]`. It is empty when no list was cut. A failed job of a merge request whose failed tests were cut has `truncated: ["failed_tests"]`. Entries in `linked_issues` and `linked_merge_requests` are ordered by ID and have `type`, `id` (a string), `token`, `relation` (`CLOSES`), `iid`, `project_path`, and `title`. Every failure after a lookup starts returns the same `not_found` error, whether the record is missing or the user cannot read it. With `expand`, the request runs at most one graph query, using the `context_for_review`, `context_for_issue`, or `context_for_job` named query. Other types return `expansion_unsupported_type`. A request that runs one query is billed as one query. A failure of the expansion never fails the summary. `expansion.query` has the `name` and `parameters` of the query. It is present on a result and on every error except `expansion_unsupported_type`, including when no query ran. After `outside_graph_scope`, a rerun is billed and returns nothing. `expansion.error.code` is one of: `expansion_unsupported_type`, when the type has no expansion query; `outside_graph_scope`, when the entity is outside the part of the graph the user can query, which is a group where the user is not at least a Reporter or a group where Orbit is not turned on, and no query runs and nothing is billed; `billing_namespace_required`, with `message`, `deep_link` to the preferences of the user, and `candidates`, the groups the user can select, matching the `422` response of `POST /api/v4/orbit/query/:name`; or `quota_exhausted`, `timeout`, or `execution_error`. If `pagination.truncated` in the graph result is `false`, a missing center node means the entity has no readable neighbors. Otherwise, the result is unknown. With `response_format=llm`, the response is `text/plain`. Each entity starts with its scalar fields, then its graph in TOON format under an indented `graph:` label, before longer blocks such as the description. A graph with no nodes is left out, and a failed expansion is a single `graph_error=<code>` line. When a list in an entity is cut, the entity includes a `truncated=` line right after its scalar fields that names the incomplete lists, for example `truncated=reviewers,changed_files`. A failed job whose failed tests were cut has its own `truncated=failed_tests` line. This feature was introduced in GitLab 19.6.
Executes a query against the Orbit gRPC service. For `response_format` `llm` and `gql`, the response is `text/plain`.

Executes a server-defined named query against the Orbit gRPC service. Orbit defines its named queries on the server, so they stay in step with the query language and the schema. For programmatic use, this endpoint is preferred over `POST /orbit/query`. The GraphQL field `Query.orbit.queryTemplates` lists the named queries. Each query template has a `name`, a `description`, and the GQL `query` it runs. The `name` of a query template is passed as `:name` in the path. Requires a JSON request body: form encoding stringifies nested parameter values, which the per-query parameter schemas reject. This endpoint can return the same errors as `POST /orbit/query`.

parameters.description: Named query identifier
parameters.name: name

get.description: Lists the Orbit skills deployed with the connected knowledge graph service. The response includes an `ETag` header derived from the sorted skill names and versions, and a `Cache-Control` header set to `private, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. Sending the `ETag` value in the `If-None-Match` request header revalidates the list. A matching value returns `304 Not Modified` with no response body. This feature was introduced in GitLab 19.5.

Retrieves a complete deployed Orbit skill tree. HEAD requests retrieve only skill metadata. The response includes a `Cache-Control` header set to `private, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, and an `ETag` header set to `"<version>"`. Sending the current `ETag` value in the `If-None-Match` request header revalidates a cached skill tree. A matching value returns `304 Not Modified` with no response body. This feature was introduced in GitLab 19.5.

get.description: Retrieves a UTF-8 file from a deployed Orbit skill as raw text. It fetches `SKILL.md` directly or follows relative links to files in the same skill tree. The response is the file content, not a JSON object. Markdown files (`.md`) have the content type `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`. Other files have the content type `text/plain; charset=utf-8`. The endpoint never returns a skill file as HTML. Only exact paths listed in the skill manifest are available. Unknown paths return `404 Not Found`. A path with a `.` segment returns `404 Not Found`. A path with a `..` segment returns `400 Bad Request`. Malformed paths can return `400 Bad Request`. API error responses are JSON, rather than raw file content. Requests blocked by path traversal middleware can return a plain-text error. The response includes a strong `ETag` from the SHA-256 of the file and a `Cache-Control` header set to `private, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. Sending the `ETag` in `If-None-Match` returns `304 Not Modified` when the file is unchanged. `HEAD` returns the same headers without a body. This feature was introduced in GitLab 19.5.

get.description:
Introduced in GitLab 18.11.

Searches indexed project code using semantic (meaning-based) similarity rather than
keyword matching. Use this when you do not know the exact symbol or file name, or
to discover how a behavior is implemented across the codebase.

Primary use cases:
- When you do not know the exact symbol or file path
- To see how a behavior or feature is implemented across the codebase
- To discover related implementations (clients, jobs, workers)

How to use:
- Provide a concise, specific query with concrete keywords
- Use directory_path to narrow scope (e.g. "app/services/")
- Prefer precise intent over broad terms

Results are grouped by file. Each file includes merged line ranges with content
and a relevance score (0.0-1.0). The response includes an overall confidence
level (high/medium/low/unknown) based on score distribution. Results are
filtered by Duo context exclusion settings.

Requires semantic code search to be enabled and indexed for the project namespace.

parameters.name: q

parameters.name: directory_path

parameters.description: Number of nearest neighbours to retrieve internally (default: 64). Higher values improve recall at the cost of latency.
parameters.name: knn

parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 20).
parameters.name: limit

404.description: Not found - project not found or semantic code search unavailable

422.description: Unprocessable entity - project has no embeddings

503.description: Service unavailable - search backend timed out

patch.description:
Sets the status of a specified external control. Use this operation to inform GitLab that a control has
passed, failed, or does not apply to the project. Controls with the `not_applicable` status do not count as
passed or failed.

Requests must use HMAC, timestamp, and nonce authentication, with these headers:

| Header | Required | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `X-Gitlab-Timestamp` | Yes | Current Unix timestamp. Requests 15 seconds old or older are rejected. |
| `X-Gitlab-Nonce` | Yes | Random string of exactly 32 characters, to prevent replay attacks. |
| `X-Gitlab-Hmac-Sha256` | Yes | HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request. |

To compute the HMAC-SHA256 signature:

1. Concatenate these values in this order: the `X-Gitlab-Timestamp` value, the `X-Gitlab-Nonce` value,
   the entire path of the request, and the `status` value formatted as `status=<status>`.
1. Compute the HMAC-SHA256 of the concatenated string with your secret key.

This feature was introduced in GitLab 17.11.

parameters.description: ID or URL-encoded path of the project.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: ID of the control.
parameters.name: control_id

If the status is `failed`, `started`, or `finished`, the `failed_relations` array might list relations that failed to import because of unrecoverable errors or because retries were exhausted, for example after query timeouts. The `id` of each `failed_relations` element references the failure record, not the relation. The `failed_relations` array is capped at 100 items. get.description: Retrieves the artifacts archive for the latest successful job on a specified branch or tag. The latest successful pipeline is determined by its creation time. The start or end time of individual jobs does not affect which pipeline is the latest. When `search_recent_successful_pipelines` is `true`, the search includes up to 100 recent successful pipelines for the ref. Otherwise, for parent and child pipelines, artifacts are searched in hierarchical order from parent to child. If both parent and child pipelines have a job with the same name, the artifact from the parent pipeline is returned. The pipeline must have completed with a `success` status, so any manual jobs in it must either complete successfully or have `allow_failure: true` set. On GitLab.com, the request might redirect through a CDN, so clients must follow redirects, for example with the cURL `--location` option.

post.description: Approves a specified merge request. The currently authenticated user must be an eligible approver. The `sha` parameter ensures you are approving the current version of the merge request. If defined, the value must match the merge request’s HEAD commit SHA, and the diff must not have changed since a version with that SHA, for example after a target branch change. Otherwise returns a `409 Conflict` response. An approval sent immediately after the merge request is created can come before its commit is processed, and a new commit can then reset the approval. To avoid this, wait until `detailed_merge_status` is not `checking` or `approvals_syncing` and the merge request diff has a `patch_id_sha`, or send `sha`. With `sha`, GitLab records the approved version even before a diff exists, so a later push does not reset the approval. The response has the same attributes as retrieving the approval state, which depend on the edition.

post.description: Creates a tag in the repository that points to a specified reference. This endpoint is rate-limited for each project. The default is 100 requests every 30 minutes, configurable with the `tags_create_limit` application setting. Set the limit to `0` to disable it. The limit is shared between this endpoint, the GraphQL `tagCreate` mutation, tag creation in the UI, and the `/tag` quick action. The limit applies to the project, so you can receive `429 Too Many Requests` after other users of the project reach the limit. The type of tag created determines the contents of `created_at`, `target`, and `message`. For annotated tags, `created_at` contains the timestamp of tag creation, `message` contains the annotation, and `target` contains the ID of the tag object. For lightweight tags, `created_at` and `message` are null, and `target` contains the commit ID.

post.description: Creates or updates the status of a commit represented by a job in an `external` stage. If the commit is associated with a merge request, target the commit in the merge request source branch. The job is added to the newest matching pipeline for the commit. If no matching pipeline exists, a new pipeline is created with `CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE: external`. When duplicate pipelines exist for the same commit, the newest one receives the status. If the matching pipeline exceeds the maximum number of jobs in a pipeline, a `422` error is returned when `pipeline_id` is specified. Otherwise, a new pipeline is created. If an update is already in progress for the same SHA and ref, a `409` error is returned, and the request can be retried.

tags.description:
Use this API to interact with access tokens including:

- [Personal access tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/personal_access_tokens/).
- [Group access tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/settings/group_access_tokens/).
- [Project access tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/settings/project_access_tokens/).
- [Impersonation tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/authentication/#impersonation-tokens).

To self-rotate a group or project access token, authenticate with that token and use the `self`
keyword in the request URL, for example `POST /projects/:id/access_tokens/self/rotate`. The token
must have the `api` or `self_rotate` scope.

When you rotate a token, GitLab links the new token to the previous one. These connected tokens form
a token family. If a rotation request authenticates with a token that was already revoked, all active
tokens in the same token family are revoked.
tags.name: Access tokens

All endpoints require authentication. To manage the approval rules of an individual merge request,
use the [merge request approvals API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/merge_request_approvals/).

Group approval rules apply to all protected branches of projects in the group. The group approval
rules endpoints are behind a feature flag named `approval_group_rules`, disabled by default.

Some endpoints return [Sigstore bundles](https://docs.sigstore.dev/about/bundle/) in the response.
For attestations that use the `SIGSTORE` attestation method, you can verify these bundles with the

Use this API to list and retrieve the
[audit events](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/compliance/audit_events/) recorded for an instance or a group.

> [!warning]
> Offset-based pagination for the audit event list endpoints was
> [deprecated](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/186194) in GitLab 17.8 and is
> planned for removal in GitLab 20.0. Use keyset-based pagination instead. This change is a breaking change.

Instance audit event endpoints require administrator access. Group audit event endpoints return the
audit events of all users to users with the Owner role, and only the events of their own actions to
users with the Developer or Maintainer role.

Requests to these endpoints are subject to configurable rate limits: per user for instance audit
events, and per user and group for group audit events.

Use this API to manage [emoji reactions](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/emoji_reactions/).

GitLab objects that accept emoji reactions are called awardables.
You can react with emoji on the following resources:

- [Epics](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/epics/)
- [Issues](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/issues/)
- [Merge requests](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/)
- [Snippets](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/snippets/)
- [Comments](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/emoji_reactions/#emoji-reactions-for-comments)

To react to a comment (also known as a note), use the emoji reaction endpoints for comments. They
work the same way for issues, merge requests, and snippets: use `issue_iid`, `merge_request_iid`,
or `snippet_id` in the path to identify the parent resource.
tags.name: Award emoji

tags.description:
Use this API to manage badges for [projects](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/badges/) and [groups](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/badges/#group-badges).

## Placeholders

Badges support placeholders that are replaced in real time in both the link and image URL.
The following placeholders are available:

- `%{project_path}`: replaced by the project path.
- `%{project_title}`: replaced by the project title.
- `%{project_name}`: replaced by the project name.
- `%{project_id}`: replaced by the project ID.
- `%{project_namespace}`: replaced by the project's namespace full path.
- `%{group_name}`: replaced by the project's top-level group name.
- `%{gitlab_server}`: replaced by the project's server name.
- `%{gitlab_pages_domain}`: replaced by the domain name hosting GitLab Pages.
- `%{default_branch}`: replaced by the project default branch.
- `%{commit_sha}`: replaced by the project's last commit SHA.
- `%{latest_tag}`: replaced by the project's last tag.

Group badge endpoints operate outside a project's context, so placeholder values are taken from the
group's earliest-created project. If no projects exist in the group, the URL is returned unchanged.
tags.name: Badges

tags.description:
Use this API to interact with [CI/CD jobs](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/jobs/).

A job response includes `artifacts_file` while the artifacts archive is downloadable, even after
`artifacts_expire_at` has passed. Artifacts kept by the **Keep artifacts from most recent successful
jobs** setting do not expire.

The `status` field in job responses and the `scope` parameter for filtering jobs use these values:

- `canceled`: Job was manually canceled or automatically aborted.
- `canceling`: Job is being canceled but `after_script` is running.
- `created`: Job has been created but not yet processed.
- `failed`: Job execution failed.
- `manual`: Job requires manual action to start.
- `pending`: Job is in the queue waiting for a runner.
- `preparing`: Runner is preparing the execution environment.
- `running`: Job is executing on a runner.
- `scheduled`: Job has been scheduled but execution has not started.
- `skipped`: Job was skipped due to conditions or dependencies.
- `success`: Job completed successfully.
- `waiting_for_callback`: Job is waiting for a callback from an external service.
- `waiting_for_resource`: Job is waiting for resources to become available.
tags.name: CI jobs

tags.description:
> [!warning]
> Registering a runner with a registration token is
> [deprecated](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/380872) and disabled by default in
> GitLab 17.0 and later.

Use this API to register a [runner](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/runners/) with an instance, verify its
authentication, reset its authentication token, and unregister it. GitLab Runner uses these endpoints
itself.

To create a runner, or to manage runners that already exist, use the Runners endpoints.

A runner uses two tokens:

- A registration token (legacy) registers the runner. You get it from GitLab.
- An authentication token authenticates the runner with GitLab. Registering a runner with a
  registration token returns its authentication token. You can also get one by creating a runner
  with `POST /user/runners`, or by resetting the runner's authentication token.

After you register a runner, add its authentication token to the runner's configuration file.
tags.name: CI runners
